_meta.indication: NESINA (alogliptin) is a DPP-4 inhibitor indicated as an adjunct to diet and exercise to improve glycemic control in adults with type 2 diabetes mellitus
_meta.receipt_date: December 27, 2007 (original NDA); most recent resubmission/complete response July 26, 2012

pivotal_trials.trial_name: PLC-010, a placebo-controlled monotherapy trial of alogliptin (SYR-322)
pivotal_trials.design: 26-week, double-blind, placebo-controlled monotherapy study in patients inadequately controlled on diet and exercise; randomized to NESINA 12.5 mg, NESINA 25 mg, or placebo once daily
pivotal_trials.population: Patients with type 2 diabetes with inadequate glycemic control on diet and exercise (mean baseline A1C = 8%)
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Change from Baseline (Day 1) in HbA1c at Week 26
pivotal_trials.result: NESINA 25 mg produced an adjusted mean A1C change from baseline of -0.6% versus 0 for placebo, a placebo-subtracted difference of -0.6% (95% CI -0.8, -0.3); 44% of NESINA patients vs 23% of placebo achieved A1C ≤7%

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (≥4% and more frequent than placebo) were nasopharyngitis (4.4% vs 3.0% placebo), headache (4.2% vs 2.5%), and upper respiratory tract infection (4.2% vs 2.1%). Pancreatitis occurred in 0.2% of NESINA 25 mg patients. Postmarketing reports included acute pancreatitis, serious hypersensitivity reactions, and hepatic failure.
target_moa: Alogliptin is a dipeptidyl-peptidase-IV (DPP-4) inhibitor that slows inactivation of incretin hormones (GLP-1 and GIP), increasing their concentrations and reducing fasting and postprandial glucose in a glucose-dependent manner

rems.type: No REMS is recommended at this time; a non-REMS medication guide was used to convey safety concerns over hypersensitivity, liver toxicity, and pancreatitis

advisory_committee.vote: No advisory committee meeting was held because this is not a first-in-class anti-diabetic therapy and the issues did not present novel regulatory or scientific challenges

summary.text: NESINA (alogliptin) was approved 1/25/2013 as a standard (non-priority) review NDA 505(b) for type 2 diabetes. The original NDA (received December 27, 2007) received two complete response actions — one on 26 June 2009 for inadequate cardiovascular data and one on 25 April 2012 for potential hepatotoxicity — before approval. No advisory committee was convened, no REMS was required, and a postmarketing cardiovascular outcomes trial (EXAMINE) was required.

citations.quote: Please refer to your New Drug Application (NDA) dated and received December 27, 2007, submitted under section 505(b) of the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act (FDCA) for Nesina (alogliptin) tablets, 6.25 mg, 12.5 mg, and 25 mg.

The alogliptin NDA was originally submitted on 27 December 2007 and received a complete response action on 26 June 2009. The primary deficiency in this complete response action was inadequate cardiovascular data for assessment. Takeda addressed this in a resubmission

received on 25 July 2011 for which a second complete response action was issued on 25 April 2012 due to a finding of potential hepatotoxicity. This most recent resubmission on 26 July 2012 is intended to address the liver safety concerns.
No REMS is recommended at this time.
